claims.text: Conventional W–Cu composites produced by sintering or spark plasma sintering have sharp, poorly bonded W–Cu interfaces.
Poor W–Cu interfacial bonding contributes to high thermal boundary resistance.
A nanoscale refractory HEA coating such as WMoTaNb can be introduced on W particles or at the W–Cu interface during processing.
The HEA coating will form a chemically bonded interlayer at the W–Cu interface.
The HEA coating will produce a compositionally graded interlayer between W and Cu.
The graded interlayer will reduce lattice mismatch between W and Cu.
The HEA interlayer will reduce thermal boundary resistance at the W–Cu interface.
The HEA coating will reduce phonon scattering at the W–Cu interface and improve heat transfer between the phases.
Nanocrystalline refractory HEAs can possess high thermal stability and irradiation resistance.
The structural stability and irradiation resistance of the HEA coating will preserve the W–Cu composite's mechanical integrity under fusion-relevant conditions.
HEA-type interlayers are relevant to joints between tungsten plasma-facing material and copper-alloy cooling structures in fusion reactors.
The proposed benefit should apply under high thermal flux and irradiation in fusion-reactor joint and heat-dissipation environments.
The HEA-coated W–Cu composite will have 15–30% higher bulk thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable uncoated W–Cu composite.
The HEA-coated composite will retain, or only minimally lose, mechanical strength relative to the uncoated W–Cu composite.
The HEA-coated composite will retain irradiation resistance relative to the uncoated W–Cu composite.
Uncoated W–Cu composites have lower thermal conductivity because of high W–Cu thermal boundary resistance.
Uncoated W–Cu composites possess adequate mechanical and irradiation performance.
The conductivity and durability benefit requires a uniform, nanoscale coating that is chemically compatible with both W and Cu.
Departures from the required coating thickness or composition may degrade thermal or mechanical behavior.
